# SSO + 3 roles

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:console-sso-rbac` · **Epic:** [#30](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/30) · **Tickets:** 11 (7S 4M)

The control-plane console gets its first user authentication. Today dashboard READS are open, and every dashboard WRITE already needs the shared CP bearer and fails closed (`dashboardWriteGuard`, internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, installed with `dash.SetWriteGuard`); /central/secrets is gated by `bearerOK`. There is no per-user identity and no role. With `console.auth: oidc`, humans sign in to Dex (or any OIDC issuer) with auth code + PKCE, get a server-side session, and are mapped from IdP groups to admin, editor or viewer. In oidc mode the bearer write guard is REPLACED by a session-and-CSRF guard, every dashboard read needs at least viewer, and every route is checked against a method-and-path role table that denies anything not listed; the shared tokens (WARDEN_CP_TOKEN, and the CP admin token) never open a human route. `console.auth: none` stays the default and keeps today's behaviour with a visible warning: open reads, writes gated by the CP admin bearer.

## How we build it

- Scope: CP only. Worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /healthz) keep their current bearer check and are not touched. The worker-local dashboard mount (internal/worker/worker.go, `adminMux.Handle("/dashboard/", dashSrv.Handler())`) keeps its current behaviour and its own admin-token write guard; authz wraps only the CP mount. New CP routes are registered in a new `internal/controlplane/routes.go` (architecture rule X9; existing registrations in controlplane.go stay baselined), and every new package or module needs an architecture.yaml class or S3 manifest entry.
- New package `internal/cpstate` (architecture.yaml class and zone required): one SQLite DB `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` (modernc.org/sqlite, already in go.mod), single connection with WAL and busy_timeout like internal/integration/store.go, and a forward-only `schema_migrations(id, applied_at)` table keyed by string IDs such as `sessions/0001` so features never collide. A DB that holds an unknown migration ID or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup (fail-closed). OIDC console mode requires `--state-dir`. The DB is opened in internal/controlplane/run.go (cmd/proxy/controlplane.go is a thin wrapper that already forwards `--state-dir`).
- CP-local `console:` block (`json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire): `auth: none|oidc`, `oidc: {issuer, clientID (default warden-console), clientSecretEnv, redirectURL, scopes, internalIssuerURL}` (`internalIssuerURL` optional, e.g. `http://dex:5556`; a plain-http issuer is accepted only with it, the W-P1-VRFY-12 rule), `roles: {admin, editor, viewer: [groups]}`, `session: {idle: 1h, absolute: 12h}` (fixed defaults). The CP reads it only from the operator-owned `--config` file, never from the `<state-dir>/config.yaml` copy, which is seeded once (`seedServedConfig` in internal/controlplane/run.go) and rewritten by the dashboard writers. With `--state-dir` set, a differing console block in the served copy is ignored with a warning; without `--state-dir` the CP serves and edits `--config` in place (oidc requires `--state-dir`, so this only concerns none mode).
- Login: `GET /auth/login` stores state, nonce, an S256 PKCE verifier and the `next` path in a cpstate `oidc_pending` row (10 min TTL, single use, capped) bound to the browser by a short-lived login cookie. `GET /auth/callback` consumes the row atomically, exchanges the code with golang.org/x/oauth2 (dependency added by W-P1-VRFY-12) through the shared W-P1-VRFY-12 HTTP client (discovery and the code exchange go to `internalIssuerURL` when set, while the issuer, redirects and tokens stay public), and verifies the ID token with a new `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier`, a thin wrapper over the W-P1-VRFY-01 OIDC verifier, that checks aud contains clientID, azp equals clientID when present or when aud has several entries, the nonce, RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew. The console uses its own Dex client `warden-console`, separate from the `warden` agent-token client. The identity key is (iss, sub); email is for display only.
- Degraded modes: OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff, so a Dex outage never stops the CP from starting or serving workers. While the IdP is unreachable only /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`; existing sessions keep working. Session expiry uses the CP clock only, and sessions survive CP restarts. The IdP-down admin path is break-glass (p1-breakglass).
- Sessions: a fresh 32-byte random id on every login, stored only as sha256 in `sessions`. Cookie `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https; plain `warden_console` only for an http redirectURL on a loopback host, with a warning. Secure follows the redirectURL scheme, not the local listener, so a TLS-terminating ingress works. The CSRF token is an HMAC of the raw session id, sent in `X-Warden-CSRF` on every non-GET request together with an Origin check against the redirectURL origin.
- Roles: the session stores the IdP groups, and the role is recomputed on every request from the current `console.roles` (admin > editor > viewer). A login whose groups match no role creates no session. Admins can list and revoke sessions. IdP group changes take effect at the next login, so the 12h absolute lifetime bounds offboarding lag unless an admin revokes earlier.
- Authz: `dashboard.Routes()` exports every {method, path, action} the dashboard registers. A CP middleware applies a table keyed by {method, path} giving the minimum role and an action name (reused by p1-admin-audit); rows are a struct so later features add fields (Target, Audited, Scope). In oidc mode EVERY dashboard route needs a session: dashboard reads are open today, but oidc mode requires viewer for every GET. Viewer: every GET, plus POST query and audit/verify. Editor: POST query/generate (it spends LLM tokens; limited to 10 per minute per session by W-P1-SSO-10), POST/PUT policy and detection, and settings writes that touch only editor fields (W-P1-SSO-10; until then settings writes are admin-only, fail-closed). Admin: POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore, /central/secrets (W-P1-SSO-06) and sessions (W-P1-SSO-08). A {method, path} not in the table is denied, and a coverage test fails on any route missing from it. In oidc mode the guard installed with `dash.SetWriteGuard` is a session-and-CSRF guard that replaces `dashboardWriteGuard()`, so the bearer no longer opens writes; in none mode the bearer guard and open reads are unchanged and the authz middleware is not installed.
- Settings writes are authorized per field (W-P1-SSO-10). Editor may change only advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents and cacheTTLSeconds (the set lives in internal/config so other features share it). Any other difference from the live SettingsWire (llmProviders, secrets, explore, judge, observability, mcp, identity, and fields added later) needs admin, because those can change where workers send real credentials, and a change to any `agents[].identity` value needs admin too. A denial returns 403 with the field names.
- The request Principal is `{Kind: session|breakglass|apikey, Iss, Sub, Email, Groups, AuthMethod}`, so p1-breakglass, p1-admin-audit and p2 API keys reuse the same table. In oidc mode WARDEN_CP_TOKEN and the CP admin token open no /dashboard/* or /central/secrets route; WARDEN_CP_TOKEN stays valid on worker routes until p1-worker-tokens.
- Back-compat: a missing `console` block means `auth: none`; the console stays as today (open reads, bearer-gated writes) and compose recipes keep working. none mode logs a startup warning ("dashboard reads are unauthenticated; writes need the shared token"), `/dashboard/api/setup` returns `authMode` (none|oidc), the UI shows a banner, and a new `--require-console-auth` flag refuses to start in none mode. Logs carry `console_login`, `console_logout`, `console_authz_denied` and `console_session_revoked` records, never tokens, codes, cookies or secret values.
- Session fixation and role drift, stated so a later refactor cannot regress them: the session id is minted server-side after successful authentication and is never accepted from the client; the login callback sets the cookie HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (Secure, `__Host-` prefixed on an https console origin) and rotates away any session cookie the request carried. Roles are computed from the groups in the login token and stored with the session; the role is re-derived on each request from the current `console.roles`, but a user demoted in the IdP keeps their console role until the session's idle or absolute expiry. The admin session revoke API (W-P1-SSO-08) is the documented manual control; the roles docs (W-P1-SSO-11) say so.
- UI: internal/dashboard/index.html already wraps writes with a bearer prompt (token asked once, kept in sessionStorage, retried after 401). In oidc mode (`/auth/me` returns 200) the UI never prompts for a token and sends `X-Warden-CSRF`; in none mode the existing bearer prompt stays unchanged (W-P1-SSO-09).
- Test layers: unit tests with a fake OIDC provider (httptest) and SessionStore.Create for most tickets; the real-Dex console proof is the L2 test W-P1-SSO-07 on the shared identity stack from p1-dex (W-P1-DEX-04). test/integration is not used.
- Logout is local: `POST /auth/logout` deletes the Warden session only; the IdP session remains, so the next login can be silent, and no `id_token_hint` is sent because no IdP token is stored. Removing a person's access is the block list's job (W-P1-BLOCK-07, W-P1-BLOCK-05).

## Done when

On a CP started with `console.auth: oidc` in --config, an https redirectURL and an existing --state-dir: an unauthenticated request, or one carrying only the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN or CP admin bearer, gets 401 on every /dashboard/api/* route (reads included) and on /central/secrets, while workers keep pulling /policy. An LDAP user in warden-viewers can read every tab but gets 403 on POST /dashboard/api/policy and POST /dashboard/api/secretstore. A warden-editors user can edit policy and toggle DLP but gets 403 when a settings change touches llmProviders or the secrets backend. Only warden-admins can edit integrations, LLM providers and secrets, and can revoke a live session, which then gets 401. A POST without a matching X-Warden-CSRF header gets 403. The session id is minted server-side after authentication, differs from any cookie the callback request carried, and is set HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and (on https) Secure with the `__Host-` prefix. The CP still starts and serves workers with Dex stopped, and a route-coverage test fails if any dashboard route has no authz entry. In `console.auth: none` the console is as today: open reads, writes gated by the CP admin bearer. The CP container reaches Dex through `console.oidc.internalIssuerURL` while the browser is sent to the public issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` (no hosts entry, no test-only dialer). Proven by unit tests per ticket and by `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestConsoleSSO` (W-P1-SSO-07).

### 1/11 · W-P1-SSO-01

**Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#31](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/31)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). Console sessions, the pending-login table, and later admin audit, policy versions, worker tokens and backups all need durable control-plane state. This foundation ticket (#31) creates the new package `internal/cpstate`: one SQLite DB at `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` and a forward-only migration runner that each feature store registers into. It has no dependencies and ships only the runner and test migrations: `oidc_pending` comes with W-P1-SSO-03 and `sessions` with W-P1-SSO-04. Siblings: SSO-02 (config), SSO-04 (sessions). Out of scope: any table, any route, any console behaviour.

What to build: This ticket ships only the runner and test migrations: `oidc_pending` comes in W-P1-SSO-03 and `sessions` in W-P1-SSO-04. It follows the single-connection modernc pattern already used in internal/integration/store.go and internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go, so it is small. Admin audit, policy versions, worker tokens and backups build on this file. Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml; new HTTP routes are registered in a routes.go (rule X9). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- API: `Open(ctx, path string, migs []Migration) (*DB, error)`, `(*DB).Close() error`, `(*DB).SQL() *sql.DB`, with `Migration{ID string; SQL string}`. `OpenReadOnly(ctx, path)` opens the file with `mode=ro`, applies no migrations, still runs quick_check and the unknown-ID check, and is what offline readers such as W-P1-AAUD-04 use. IDs are unique strings such as `sessions/0001`, so migrations from different features never collide.
- `schema_migrations(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)`. Each migration and its row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls back both.
- Downgrade guard: if the DB holds a migration ID the binary does not register, Open returns an error naming that ID and leaves the file unchanged.
- Connection settings match the repo: `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` and DSN pragmas journal_mode(WAL), busy_timeout(5000), foreign_keys(1). The file is created with mode 0600.
- Fail-closed: a file that is not a database or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup with an error naming the path and a hint to restore from backup or move the file aside.
- The DB is opened in `internal/controlplane/run.go` (the control-plane run function; cmd/proxy/controlplane.go is a thin wrapper and already forwards `--state-dir`), only when a state dir is set, and is passed in a new `controlplane.Config.State *cpstate.DB` field; without `--state-dir` State is nil and CP behaviour is unchanged. The DB is closed after the HTTP server drains.
- One startup log line with fields `db` and `applied` (migration IDs). Row contents are never logged.
- Architecture gate: `internal/cpstate` gets exactly one class (it does SQLite I/O: the repository class, like internal/integration) and a zone (control plane) in architecture.yaml; modernc.org/sqlite is already in the S3 manifest, so no module entry is needed. The package has a _test.go (rule C3).
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/cpstate/cpstate.go (new) with DB, Migration and Open, using sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)") and SetMaxOpenConns(1) as in internal/integration/store.go; chmod the file to 0600 after create.
2. In Open, run `PRAGMA quick_check` and return a wrapped error when it does not return `ok`.
3. Create internal/cpstate/migrate.go (new): create schema_migrations, read applied IDs, refuse unknown IDs, then apply each missing Migration in the order passed, one transaction each.
4. In internal/controlplane/run.go, when stateDir != "", call cpstate.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(stateDir, "warden-cp.db"), nil) and set the new controlplane.Config.State field (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go); close it after shutdown. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go needs no change.
5. Add internal/cpstate/cpstate_test.go (new) with two migration sets, an unknown-ID DB, a failing migration, a garbage file and 50 concurrent writers.
6. Tests: internal/controlplane/run_test.go gets TestRunCreatesStateDB (warden-cp.db exists with mode 0600) and TestRunCorruptStateDB (a garbage file makes Run return an error naming the path); cmd/proxy/commands_test.go keeps a thin exit-code case.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a DB with migration `t/0001`, when Open runs with {`t/0001`, `t/0002`}, then only `t/0002` is applied: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestMigrateAppliesOnlyNew`
- [ ] Given a DB that holds `t/0003`, when a binary registering only `t/0001` and `t/0002` opens it, then Open fails naming `t/0003` and the file bytes are unchanged: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestMigrateRefusesUnknownID`
- [ ] Given a migration whose SQL fails, when Open runs, then its ID is not recorded and earlier tables are intact
- [ ] Given 50 goroutines doing 100 inserts each, when run with -race, then none returns SQLITE_BUSY: `go test -race ./internal/cpstate -run TestConcurrentWriters`
- [ ] Given a warden-cp.db of random bytes, when the control plane starts, then Run returns an error naming the path and the command exits non-zero: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestRunCorruptStateDB` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneCorruptStateDB`
- [ ] Without --state-dir, existing CP tests pass unchanged: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane`
- [ ] Given an existing DB, when OpenReadOnly is used and a write is attempted, then the write fails and the file's bytes and mtime are unchanged: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestOpenReadOnly`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes with the new package class and zone, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 2/11 · W-P1-SSO-02

**Parse and validate the CP-local console config block**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#32](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/32)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#32) adds the CP-local `console:` config block that every later console ticket reads: strict parsing, validation and a pure `RoleFor(groups)` used at login and on every request. It has no dependencies. Siblings: SSO-01 (state DB), SSO-03/04/05 (login, sessions, enforcement), SSO-06 (removes the temporary oidc guard and adds `--require-console-auth`). Out of scope: login, sessions, any route. The CP reads the block only from the operator-owned `--config` file, because the `--state-dir` copy is seeded once and rewritten by the dashboard, so edits there would be ignored or could be changed from the UI. Break-glass fields are left to W-P1-OPS1-01. Until W-P1-SSO-06 lands, the control plane refuses to start with `console.auth: oidc`, so no build ever runs with login routes but no enforcement. In `console.auth: none` the console keeps today's behaviour: dashboard reads are open and every dashboard write is gated by the CP admin bearer through `dashboardWriteGuard` (internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, fail-closed, constant-time, via `dashboard.SetWriteGuard`); that bearer is the separate CP admin token (`--admin-token-env`) delivered by the worker-tokens work, and until it lands the existing shared `--token-env` bearer fills the role. In `console.auth: oidc` sessions and CSRF replace it: the shared tokens never open a human route.

**Requirements**

- internal/config/console.go (new): `ConsoleConfig{Auth string; OIDC ConsoleOIDC; Roles ConsoleRoles; Session ConsoleSession}`, `ConsoleOIDC{Issuer, ClientID, ClientSecretEnv, RedirectURL string; Scopes []string; InternalIssuerURL string}` (`internalIssuerURL`, optional: the origin the CP container uses to reach the IdP, for example `http://dex:5556`; there is no insecure-issuer key), `ConsoleRoles{Admin, Editor, Viewer []string}`, `ConsoleSession{Idle, Absolute time.Duration}`, and `type Role int` with RoleViewer < RoleEditor < RoleAdmin.
- Defaults: an absent block means Auth=none; clientID defaults to `warden-console`, the reference console client from W-P1-DEX-01; Scopes default to [openid, email, profile, groups]; Idle 1h; Absolute 12h (the decided defaults; not 8h/24h). Any Auth value other than none or oidc is a validation error.
- oidc validation: issuer, clientSecretEnv and redirectURL are required and clientID must be non-empty after defaulting; the issuer must be https unless `internalIssuerURL` is set (the http-issuer rule of W-P1-VRFY-12, applied here without importing internal/identity: a plain-http issuer is the dev profile and needs an internal issuer URL); `internalIssuerURL`, when set, must be an absolute http or https URL with an empty path or `/`, no userinfo, query or fragment, and needs a non-empty issuer; redirectURL must be https unless its host is loopback; redirectURL must be absolute and end in /auth/callback; at least one admin group; 0 < Idle <= Absolute <= 168h.
- `Policy.Console ConsoleConfig` has `json:"-"`, so it never appears on policyWire or SettingsWire. rawConfig accepts the `console:` key under KnownFields(true), so workers and the served copy still parse.
- New `config.LoadConsole(path string) (ConsoleConfig, error)`. The control plane calls it on `--config` (not on the served path). With `--state-dir` set, if the served copy holds a different console block it logs a warning and ignores it; without `--state-dir` the CP serves `--config` itself and there is no second copy. Changing the block needs a CP restart.
- `func (c ConsoleConfig) RoleFor(groups []string) (Role, bool)` is pure; the highest matching role wins. Group matching is exact and case-sensitive.
- At startup in oidc mode: an empty `os.Getenv(clientSecretEnv)` or a missing `--state-dir` is a fatal error, logs name the env var but never its value, a plain-http issuer with an `internalIssuerURL` logs a dev-profile warning, and a temporary guard refuses oidc with "console oidc enforcement is not available in this build" (removed by W-P1-SSO-06, the ticket that also secures /central/secrets, so no build serves oidc login while any human route still accepts the shared bearer).

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/config/console.go (new) with the types, defaults, Role, RoleFor and validateConsole.
2. In internal/config/config.go add an unexported rawConsole and `Console *rawConsole `yaml:"console"`` to rawConfig, convert it next to the Detection assignment into Policy.Console, and call validateConsole from validate().
3. Add LoadConsole(path) in internal/config/console.go, reusing the strict decoder to read only the console node.
4. In internal/controlplane/run.go add resolveConsole(configPath, servedPath, stateDir, getenv) (new, next to seedServedConfig at run.go:308): load from the `--config` path, compare with the served copy's block only when a state dir is set, check the secret env and --state-dir, apply the temporary oidc guard, and pass the result in a new controlplane.Config.Console field. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go stays a thin wrapper.
5. Add a commented example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml: an https production block and a compose block with issuer http://localhost:5556/dex, internalIssuerURL http://dex:5556 (the CP runs in a container where `localhost` is itself), clientID warden-console, clientSecretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET and redirectURL https://localhost:7070/auth/callback, matching the W-P1-DEX-01 client.
6. Tests: internal/config/console_test.go (new); internal/controlplane/console_wire_test.go (new) for policyWire (controlplane.go) and SettingsWire; writer preservation in internal/controlplane; resolveConsole cases in internal/controlplane/run_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Table tests cover a valid oidc block, a missing admin group, an http issuer without `internalIssuerURL` (rejected), the same with `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` (accepted), an https issuer without it (accepted), an internalIssuerURL with a path, a query or a non-http scheme, or set with an empty issuer (rejected), an http redirectURL on a non-loopback host (rejected) and on 127.0.0.1 (accepted), idle > absolute (rejected), an unknown auth value (rejected) and RoleFor precedence: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestConsoleConfig|TestRoleFor'`
- [ ] Given a Policy with a fully set Console, when policyWire and SettingsWire are marshalled, then neither JSON contains `console`, `clientSecretEnv` or `roles`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestConsoleNotOnWire`
- [ ] Given a served config with a console block, when WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations and WriteDetection each persist an edit, then the console node is byte-identical: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWritersPreserveConsoleBlock`
- [ ] Given --config with console.auth=oidc and an existing --state-dir whose config.yaml has no console block, when resolveConsole runs, then it returns the --config block: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestResolveConsoleFromConfigFlag`
- [ ] Given oidc mode with an empty client secret env var, when resolveConsole runs, then it fails naming the variable and captured logs hold no secret value: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestResolveConsoleSecretEnv`
- [ ] Given an existing config with no console block, when it is parsed, then Console.Auth is "none" and existing config tests pass: `go test ./internal/config`
- [ ] Given console.auth=oidc, when the control plane starts, then it refuses with "console oidc enforcement is not available in this build" until W-P1-SSO-06: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestResolveConsoleTemporaryOIDCGuard`.
- [ ] `grep -rniE 'allowInsecure[I]ssuer' internal/config configs` prints nothing, and a config that still sets the removed insecure-issuer key (the old `allowInsecure` + `Issuer` spelling) is rejected by the strict parser: `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsoleNoInsecureKey`.

### 3/11 · W-P1-SSO-03

**Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#33](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/33)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#33) is the login half of console SSO: `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` on the CP mux in oidc mode, using authorization code with S256 PKCE, a browser-bound single-use pending row in cpstate, and strict ID token checks. It depends on W-P1-SSO-04 (SessionStore.Create, which in turn builds on SSO-01 cpstate and SSO-02 console config/RoleFor), W-P1-VRFY-01 (the OIDC verifier) and W-P1-VRFY-12 (the shared OIDC HTTP client with the internal-origin rewrite, used for discovery and the code exchange). It adds a thin ID-token verifier to internal/identity on top of that verifier (Audience=clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], WithNonce), so the console shares its keyset, algorithm allowlist and skew handling, and uses the `warden-console` client already defined in the reference Dex config (W-P1-DEX-01). Siblings: SSO-04 (sessions), SSO-09 (logout, /auth/me, UI wrapper), SSO-05 (enforcement), SSO-06 (removes the temporary oidc startup guard). Out of scope: authorization of routes, logout, the UI. The real-Dex proof is W-P1-SSO-07.

What to build: the pending-login store, the lazy OIDC provider, the two handlers and the identity wrapper. Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml; new HTTP routes are registered in a routes.go (rule X9). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- Routes are mounted only when console.auth=oidc and Config.State is set; in none mode they return 404. They are registered in the new `internal/controlplane/routes.go` (rule X9: not in controlplane.go). `next` is accepted only as a relative path under /dashboard/ (no scheme, no `//`, no backslash), otherwise /dashboard/ is used.
- OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff in a goroutine started from Server.Start, run through the client of identity.NewHTTPClient (W-P1-VRFY-12) built from console.oidc.{issuer,internalIssuerURL} and handed to go-oidc and oauth2 with identity.WithHTTPClient, so discovery, JWKS and the code exchange reach the internal origin while the authorize redirect, the issuer and every token stay public; until it succeeds /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`, and CP startup and worker routes are unaffected.
- Migration `oidc_pending/0001`: `oidc_pending(state_hash PK, nonce, verifier, next, browser_hash, expires_at)` with a 10 min TTL. Callback consumes the row with `DELETE ... RETURNING` in one statement. Rows are swept every minute and capped at 10,000; above the cap login returns 503.
- Browser binding: /auth/login sets `__Host-warden_login` (or `warden_login` on http; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age 600) holding random bytes whose sha256 must equal browser_hash at callback; the cookie is cleared after use.
- New `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier(ctx, IDTokenConfig{Issuer, ClientID, InternalIssuerURL})` built on identity.NewOIDCVerifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 with Audience=ClientID, AllowedAZP=[ClientID] and WithNonce; it adds the OIDC Core rule that azp must be present and equal ClientID when aud has several entries. The shared client, the http-issuer rule, RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew come from the shared verifier. The callback compares the nonce in constant time.
- On success: RoleFor(groups) must match, else redirect with `login_error=no_role` and no session; groups capped at 256; SessionStore.Create issues a fresh id; offline_access is not requested and no access, refresh or ID token is stored.
- Errors redirect to `/dashboard/?login_error=<code>` with code from {state_invalid, nonce_mismatch, token_invalid, exchange_failed, idp_error, no_role, idp_unavailable}; IdP error text is never echoed.
- No Dex config change: the `warden-console` client (redirect https://localhost:7070/auth/callback, secretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET) comes from W-P1-DEX-01. Each attempt logs `msg=console_login result reason sub duration_ms`, never the code, state, verifier, nonce or tokens.
- Session fixation: the session id is minted server-side by SessionStore.Create after the ID token verified and RoleFor matched, and is never taken from the request. The callback ignores any session cookie value the request carried: the resulting cookie value always differs from it, and the old session row (if any) is deleted. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, Secure with the `__Host-` prefix when the redirectURL is https (cookie helper from W-P1-SSO-04).
- Architecture gate: add `golang.org/x/oauth2` to the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml with the layers that import it (W-P1-VRFY-12 normally adds it already; verify and skip if present, and make sure the allowed layers cover the control-plane assembly package as well), and add no new package (the handlers live in internal/controlplane; the verifier wrapper in internal/identity from W-P1-VRFY-01).
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Confirm golang.org/x/oauth2 and go-oidc v3 are already in go.mod (added by W-P1-VRFY-12; add `golang.org/x/oauth2@<exact version at least two weeks old>` only if it is missing) and run govulncheck.
2. Add internal/identity/idtoken.go (new) with NewIDTokenVerifier wrapping identity.NewOIDCVerifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 (Claims already carries Nonce and AZP), so the JWKS cache and refetch floor are shared.
3. Create internal/controlplane/oidc_pending.go (new): migration, Put, Take(stateHash) with DELETE ... RETURNING and expiry check, Count for the cap, and Sweep(now).
4. Create internal/controlplane/auth.go (new): lazy provider with backoff, oauth2.Config{ClientID, ClientSecret, RedirectURL, Scopes, Endpoint} with every call given a context made by identity.WithHTTPClient, handleLogin using oauth2.GenerateVerifier, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption and SetAuthURLParam("nonce"), and handleCallback using Exchange with oauth2.VerifierOption, then the ID-token verifier, RoleFor and SessionStore.Create.
5. Mount /auth/login and /auth/callback from the new internal/controlplane/routes.go (called by Server.Handler in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) only in oidc mode; start the discovery and sweeper goroutines in Server.Start.
6. Use the existing `warden-console` client and WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET from W-P1-DEX-01/02 in the docs example; do not edit deploy/compose/dex.
7. Add internal/controlplane/auth_test.go (new) with an httptest fake OIDC provider (discovery, JWKS, token endpoint, RSA key) and a fake clock, plus internal/identity/idtoken_test.go (new).
8. Add the architecture.yaml S3 manifest entry for golang.org/x/oauth2 (unless it already exists) and run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a fake OIDC provider, when a client follows /auth/login, the provider redirect and /auth/callback, then a sessions row exists for (iss, sub), a session cookie is set and the response redirects to `next`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCLoginEndToEnd`
- [ ] Given a replayed state, a mismatched nonce, aud=[agent-harness] only, aud=[warden-console, agent-harness] with azp=agent-harness, an expired token, or alg none/HS256, when the callback runs, then no session row is created and the redirect carries the matching login_error: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCCallbackRejects`
- [ ] Given a valid state but no matching login cookie, when the callback runs, then it fails with state_invalid
- [ ] Given next=https://evil.example or //evil.example, when login completes, then the redirect goes to /dashboard/
- [ ] Given a user whose groups match no role, when the callback runs, then no session row exists and login_error=no_role
- [ ] Given the fake provider is down at CP start, when /policy and /auth/login are requested, then /policy answers as before and /auth/login returns 503 idp_unavailable; after the provider comes up, login succeeds
- [ ] Captured logs from the end-to-end test contain none of the authorization code, verifier, nonce or raw ID token
- [ ] Given a request to /auth/callback that carries an existing session cookie value X, when login completes, then the new cookie value differs from X, the row for X is gone, and Set-Cookie has HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and (for an https redirectURL) the `__Host-` prefix and Secure: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCSessionFixation`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes with the oauth2 manifest entry and routes.go registration, and `scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck.
- [ ] Given a fake provider that listens only on an internal origin, console.oidc.issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` (nothing listens there) and `internalIssuerURL` set to the fake, when a client follows /auth/login and /auth/callback, then discovery, JWKS and the token exchange reach the fake, the /auth/login redirect `Location` uses the public issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`, the ID token's iss is the public issuer, and a session is created; without `internalIssuerURL` the same setup returns 503 `idp_unavailable` (red first): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCLoginInternalIssuer`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#411--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF; [`W-P1-VRFY-01`](identity-verification.md#112--w-p1-vrfy-01) Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config; [`W-P1-VRFY-12`](identity-verification.md#1212--w-p1-vrfy-12) Add the shared OIDC HTTP client with internal-origin rewrite and the http-issuer rule

### 4/11 · W-P1-SSO-04

**Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#34](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/34)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#34) is the session core: the `sessions` store, the middleware that puts a Principal into the request context, the session cookie and the CSRF checks. It is built and tested by calling SessionStore.Create directly, so it lands before the login flow in W-P1-SSO-03. It depends on SSO-01 (cpstate) and SSO-02 (console config). It authenticates but does not deny anything: enforcement comes in W-P1-SSO-05. It was split from the original M ticket #34: `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /auth/me` and the dashboard `api()` fetch wrapper moved to W-P1-SSO-09, because other tickets depend on the Principal and the store, not on the endpoints or the UI. Siblings: SSO-03 (login), SSO-09, SSO-05. W-P3-CSIG-05 later extracts this store into internal/webauth. Out of scope: logout, /auth/me, the UI, role checks.

What to build: the sessions migration and SessionStore, Principal, withSession and the CSRF/Origin check, the cookie helper and the sweeper. withSession is wired in oidc mode only. Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml; new HTTP routes are registered in a routes.go (rule X9). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- Migration `sessions/0001`: `sessions(id_hash PK, iss, sub, email, groups_json, auth_method, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at)` with indexes on expires_at and sub. `SessionStore` takes an injectable `now func() time.Time` and has Create, Lookup, Touch, Delete, DeleteBySub, List and SweepExpired.
- Every Create issues a fresh 32-byte crypto/rand id (base64url); only sha256(id) is stored. The CSRF token is HMAC-SHA256(raw id, "warden-csrf"), so it is never stored.
- Cookie: `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when console.oidc.redirectURL is https; `warden_console` without Secure only when redirectURL is http on a loopback host, with a startup warning. Secure is never derived from r.TLS. The cookie helper is exported inside the package for SSO-03 (login) and SSO-09 (logout).
- Idle and absolute expiry use the CP clock; last_seen_at is written at most once per minute per session; expired rows are swept every minute from Server.Start.
- `Principal{Kind, Iss, Sub, Email string; Groups []string; AuthMethod string}` with WithPrincipal and PrincipalFrom(ctx); Kind is session|breakglass|apikey so later auth methods reuse it. withSession is applied only to /dashboard/, /central/secrets and /auth/*, never to /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /healthz. `CSRFToken(rawID)` is exported for SSO-09.
- CSRF: for methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS with a session, `X-Warden-CSRF` must match in constant time and Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin; otherwise 403 `{"error":"csrf"}`.
- Out of this ticket: `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /auth/me` and the UI wrapper (W-P1-SSO-09).
- Logs show at most the first 8 hex characters of id_hash and never the cookie value or CSRF token.
- Architecture gate: new files live in internal/controlplane (no new package or module). Any route registration goes through the new internal/controlplane/routes.go (rule X9); this ticket only wraps existing mounts.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/controlplane/session.go (new): the migration, SessionStore and its methods.
2. Create internal/controlplane/principal.go (new): Principal, WithPrincipal, PrincipalFrom.
3. Create internal/controlplane/session_mw.go (new): withSession (cookie read, Lookup, expiry, Touch, Principal), the CSRF and Origin check, and the cookie helper that picks the name and flags from RedirectURL.
4. Wrap /dashboard/ and /central/secrets with withSession in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) only in oidc mode, and start SweepExpired in Server.Start.
5. Add internal/controlplane/session_test.go (new) with a fake clock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a session and a fake clock, when 1h01m pass idle the next request has no Principal, and with steady activity a request after 12h01m has none: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionExpiry`
- [ ] Given a valid session, when POST /dashboard/api/policy is sent with no X-Warden-CSRF, a wrong value, or a foreign Origin, then each gets 403 `{"error":"csrf"}` and the policy file is unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionCSRF`
- [ ] Given redirectURL https://cp.example/auth/callback, when a session is created, then Set-Cookie is `__Host-warden_console` with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax even though the test server is plain HTTP: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionCookieFlags`
- [ ] Given 10 requests within one minute, then last_seen_at is written once; and the sessions table holds the sha256 hash, never the raw id: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestSessionTouchOncePerMinute|TestSessionStoresHashOnly'`
- [ ] Given a request to /policy carrying a session cookie, when it is served, then the session store is not queried (counted with a fake store): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionNotOnWorkerRoutes`
- [ ] Each Create returns a distinct 32-byte id, and Lookup/Delete/DeleteBySub/List/SweepExpired behave per their contract: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionStore`
- [ ] Logs contain at most 8 hex characters of an id_hash and never the cookie value or CSRF token: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionLogsNoSecrets`
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 5/11 · W-P1-SSO-05

**Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#35](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/35)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#35) makes oidc mode real: every {method, path} the dashboard serves gets a minimum role and an action name, anything not listed is denied, and in oidc mode the bearer write guard (`dashboardWriteGuard`, installed with `dash.SetWriteGuard`) is replaced by a session-and-CSRF guard. Reads need at least viewer in oidc mode. In `console.auth: none` the console keeps today's behaviour: dashboard reads are open and every dashboard write is gated by the CP admin bearer through `dashboardWriteGuard` (internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, fail-closed, constant-time, via `dashboard.SetWriteGuard`); that bearer is the separate CP admin token (`--admin-token-env`) delivered by the worker-tokens work, and until it lands the existing shared `--token-env` bearer fills the role. In `console.auth: oidc` sessions and CSRF replace it: the shared tokens never open a human route. It depends on W-P1-SSO-04 only (sessions, Principal, CSRF; its tests create sessions with SessionStore.Create, so it does not need the login flow of SSO-03, and the temporary oidc startup guard from SSO-02 stays in place until SSO-06, so no build serves oidc before /central/secrets is secured). It was split from the original M ticket #35: per-field settings authorization and the query/generate rate limit moved to W-P1-SSO-10, the role-aware UI and role-matrix docs to W-P1-SSO-11. Until SSO-10 lands, settings writes are admin-only (fail-closed) and query/generate is editor without a rate limit. Other tickets add rows to this table (admin audit, API keys, worker tokens, agent registry...): rows are a struct so they can add fields. Out of scope here: /central/secrets (SSO-06), sessions admin routes (SSO-08), per-field settings (SSO-10), UI (SSO-11).

What to build: `dashboard.Routes()`, the CP authz table and `requireRole` middleware, and the oidc write guard. The dashboard registers routes by path and switches on method inside each handler, and http.ServeMux cannot list its patterns, so a static route list feeds both registration and the coverage test. Architecture gate: every new package needs exactly one class in architecture.yaml (rule L8) and a zone (Z1); every new third-party module needs an entry in the S3 `modules:` manifest of architecture.yaml; new HTTP routes are registered in a routes.go (rule X9). Run `go run ./cmd/archgen` and `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` after editing architecture.yaml.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: `type Route struct{Method, Path, Action string}` and `func Routes() []Route` listing every method each handler accepts (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE per path under /dashboard/api/ plus GET /dashboard/). `Server.Handler()` registers its mux from the same list, so the worker dashboard (internal/worker/worker.go) behaves exactly as before and a route cannot exist without a list entry.
- internal/controlplane/authz.go (new): the table keyed by {method, path} -> `authzRow{MinRole config.Role; Action string}` (a struct that later tickets extend with Target, Audited and Scope). Viewer: GET on every dashboard path, POST /dashboard/api/query, POST /dashboard/api/audit/verify. Editor: POST /dashboard/api/query/generate, POST/PUT policy, POST/PUT detection. Admin: POST/PUT settings (until W-P1-SSO-10 relaxes editor fields), POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore. A {method, path} not in the table is denied with 403 for every method, GET included (deny by default).
- `requireRole` middleware (oidc mode only): the Principal comes from withSession (SSO-04); the role is recomputed on EACH request with `console.RoleFor(principal.Groups)` against the current config. No Principal: 401 JSON `{"error":"unauthenticated"}` for /dashboard/api/*, 302 to `/auth/login?next=` for HTML. Role too low: 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"<role>"}`. The row's Action is stored on the request context (`ActionFrom(ctx)`) for W-P1-AAUD-02.
- Write guard in oidc mode: `dash.SetWriteGuard(s.sessionWriteGuard())` replaces `s.dashboardWriteGuard()` (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go, currently `dash.SetWriteGuard(s.dashboardWriteGuard())`). The session guard allows a write only when a Principal is present and CSRF was verified by withSession, else 401 / 403; it never looks at the Authorization header, so neither WARDEN_CP_TOKEN nor the CP admin bearer opens a dashboard write. An `Authorization` header on any /dashboard/* request is ignored for authentication in oidc mode.
- none mode is untouched: `dashboardWriteGuard()` (bearer, fail-closed) and open reads exactly as today; the authz middleware and session guard are not installed. The existing dashboard_auth tests pass unchanged.
- The middleware wraps only the CP mount of `dash.Handler()` (`mux.Handle("/dashboard/", ...)`), via withSession then requireRole, wired in the new `internal/controlplane/routes.go` (rule X9). /central/secrets is left to W-P1-SSO-06. The temporary oidc startup guard in internal/controlplane/run.go stays until SSO-06.
- Each denial logs `msg=console_authz_denied action role sub method path`; no tokens, cookies or bodies are logged.
- Fail-closed requirements, each with a test: no Principal -> 401/302; unlisted route -> 403; a table row missing for a registered route fails the coverage test; shared bearer on any /dashboard/* route in oidc mode -> 401; CSRF missing on a session write -> 403.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `architecture.yaml` (and the regenerated `.golangci.arch.yml`); request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go add Route and Routes() and make Handler() register from it; keep handler bodies unchanged. Add TestRoutesMatchHandler.
2. Create internal/controlplane/authz.go (new): the table, requireRole, ActionFrom, sessionWriteGuard.
3. Create internal/controlplane/routes.go (new) with the CP's new mounts and call it from Server.Handler; in oidc mode wrap `/dashboard/` with withSession then requireRole and install `sessionWriteGuard` instead of `dashboardWriteGuard`.
4. Add internal/controlplane/authz_test.go (new) with viewer, editor and admin sessions created through SessionStore.Create and a fake clock.
5. Run the existing dashboard, controlplane and worker suites to confirm none-mode and worker behaviour are unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] For every Routes() entry and every role, the status matches the table (403 versus not 403): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzMatrix`
- [ ] Given a Routes() entry with no table row, when the coverage test runs, then it fails naming the route, and a request to an unlisted path or method gets 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage` (red first: delete a row and watch it fail).
- [ ] Given oidc mode and only `Authorization: Bearer <shared or admin token>`, GET /dashboard/api/traffic and POST /dashboard/api/policy both get 401, and a viewer session with CSRF gets 200 on the GET: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOIDCModeBearerNeverOpensDashboard`
- [ ] Given a viewer, when POST /dashboard/api/secretstore or POST /dashboard/api/policy is sent, then 403 `role_required`; given no session, /dashboard/api/traffic gets 401 and /dashboard/ gets 302: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzDenials`
- [ ] Given an editor session, POST /dashboard/api/settings gets 403 `need admin` until SSO-10 (fail-closed), POST /dashboard/api/policy succeeds, and POST /dashboard/api/query/generate succeeds: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzEditorSettingsAdminOnly`
- [ ] Given console.roles moves group eng from editor to viewer and the CP restarts, when an existing eng session POSTs /dashboard/api/policy, then 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRoleRecomputed`
- [ ] Given none mode, reads are open and a write without the CP bearer is refused exactly as before: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestDashboardWriteGuard|TestNoneModeUnchanged'` and the existing dashboard_auth tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Worker dashboard tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/worker`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/archtest -run TestArchitecture` passes (routes.go registration), and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 6/11 · W-P1-SSO-06

**Require an admin session on /central/secrets and flag open consoles**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#36](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/36)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#36) finishes console enforcement. After W-P1-SSO-05, oidc mode replaces the bearer write guard on the dashboard with sessions and CSRF. The remaining human route is `/central/secrets`, today gated by bearerOK (internal/controlplane/secrets.go): in oidc mode it must require an admin session plus CSRF and ignore the bearer. It also makes none mode visible (warning, `authMode`, UI banner, `--require-console-auth`) and, being the last enforcement ticket, removes the temporary oidc startup guard from W-P1-SSO-02, so no build serves oidc login while any human route still accepts the shared bearer. It depends on SSO-05 and SSO-03 (login must exist before the guard is lifted). Siblings: SSO-08 (sessions admin), SSO-11 (UI/docs). In `console.auth: none` the console keeps today's behaviour: dashboard reads are open and every dashboard write is gated by the CP admin bearer through `dashboardWriteGuard` (internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, fail-closed, constant-time, via `dashboard.SetWriteGuard`); that bearer is the separate CP admin token (`--admin-token-env`) delivered by the worker-tokens work, and until it lands the existing shared `--token-env` bearer fills the role. In `console.auth: oidc` sessions and CSRF replace it: the shared tokens never open a human route. Out of scope: worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest keep their current bearer in both modes until the worker-token work), per-field settings authz.

What to build: the secrets authorization switch, the none-mode visibility changes, the flag, the guard removal and the migration docs.

**Requirements**

- In oidc mode handleSecrets and handleSecretByKey require an admin Principal plus CSRF (the /central/secrets mounts are wrapped with withSession in oidc mode, registered from internal/controlplane/routes.go); a request with only `Authorization: Bearer <shared token or CP admin token>` gets 401 and an editor gets 403. In none mode bearerOK behaves exactly as today.
- bearerOK keeps gating /policy and /control/heartbeat, and analytics.NewIngestHandler keeps gating /central/ingest, unchanged in both modes until W-P1-WTOK-02.
- In oidc mode an Authorization header on /dashboard/* is ignored for authentication; only the session counts.
- None mode logs one startup warning ("console.auth=none: dashboard reads are unauthenticated; writes need the admin bearer"); setupResponse (internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go) gains `authMode` (`none` or `oidc`), and index.html shows a persistent banner when it is none.
- New flag `--require-console-auth` (default false) on the control-plane command makes the control plane refuse to start when console.auth is none.
- Update docs/control-plane.md, section "Dashboard writes need the control-plane token" (existing; it currently says dashboard writes need the shared worker token `--token-env`): replace that shared-token statement with the true none-mode statement (dashboard reads are open; every dashboard write is gated by the CP admin bearer, fail closed); add a "Migrating from none to oidc" subsection (set `console.auth: oidc`, the oidc block, client secret env and `--state-dir`, then verify login and roles); and state that scripts calling /central/secrets with the shared bearer stop working in oidc mode, because secret writes then need an admin session plus CSRF and go through the admin secretstore tab until scoped API keys exist.
- Remove the temporary guard added by W-P1-SSO-02 ("console oidc enforcement is not available in this build", internal/controlplane/run.go resolveConsole): oidc mode now starts. A test pins that oidc starts with a valid block, a secret and a state dir.

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/controlplane/secrets.go add secretsAuthOK(r) (new): oidc mode checks PrincipalFrom(r.Context()) for admin, else falls back to bearerOK; use it in handleSecrets and handleSecretByKey.
2. Wrap /central/secrets and /central/secrets/ in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) with withSession in oidc mode; leave /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest as they are.
3. In internal/dashboard add SetAuthMode(string) (new) and the authMode field on setupResponse; the CP sets it from Config.Console.Auth.
4. In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go add the --require-console-auth flag (thin: it only passes a bool into internal/controlplane Params); the none-mode warning and the refusal live in internal/controlplane/run.go. Remove the temporary oidc guard there.
5. Update internal/dashboard/index.html for the banner and docs/control-plane.md (section "Dashboard writes need the control-plane token") as above.
6. Add tests in internal/controlplane/secrets_test.go, internal/dashboard and cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given oidc mode, when GET or POST /central/secrets is sent with only the shared bearer, then 401; with an admin session and CSRF, 2xx; with an editor session, 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSecretsOIDCMode`
- [ ] Given oidc mode, when GET /dashboard/api/traffic is sent with only the shared bearer, then 401
- [ ] Given either mode, when a worker uses the shared bearer on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, then responses match current behaviour: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSharedTokenWorkerRoutes`
- [ ] Given none mode, when the CP starts, then the warning is logged exactly once and GET /dashboard/api/setup returns authMode "none"; with --require-console-auth it exits non-zero: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestNoneModeWarning|TestRequireConsoleAuth'` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRequireConsoleAuth`
- [ ] Given none mode, existing tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy`
- [ ] Given a valid oidc block, an existing --state-dir and the client secret in the environment, when the CP starts, then it serves (the temporary guard is gone): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestResolveConsoleOIDCStarts`.
- [ ] In none mode GET /dashboard/api/traffic stays open and POST /dashboard/api/policy without the bearer is refused, as before: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestNoneModeUnchanged`.
- [ ] The docs carry the new statements: `grep -n "Migrating from none to oidc" docs/control-plane.md` matches, `grep -n "/central/secrets" docs/control-plane.md` matches the oidc-mode note, and the old claim is gone: `grep -n "same token workers use for" docs/control-plane.md` prints nothing.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 7/11 · W-P1-SSO-07

**Add the L2 Dex-backed console SSO end-to-end test**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#230](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/230)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). Every other ticket in this feature tests against an httptest fake IdP. This ticket (#230) proves the feature's done-when against the real reference stack: Dex with the seeded LDAP users and a CP in oidc mode. It is an L2 test in `test/e2e/identity` on the shared identity stack built by W-P1-DEX-04 (compose project, Dex, LDAP, certs, host ports, helpers), not a test/integration rig and not a WARDEN_IT_DEX switch, and not an L1 scenario (L1 has no real Dex). Depends on SSO-06 (oidc starts, /central/secrets secured), SSO-08 (session revoke) and DEX-04. Out of scope: any product code; the stack and Dex runtime proofs are in p1-dex.

What to build: the console block in `configs/config.e2e-identity-cp.yaml` and the test file `test/e2e/identity/console_sso_test.go` (tests `TestConsoleSSO*`).

**Requirements**

- Edit `configs/config.e2e-identity-cp.yaml` (created by W-P1-DEX-04): add `console:` with auth oidc, issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`, `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` (the CP runs in a container where `localhost` is itself, so it reaches Dex through the internal origin while the issuer string stays public), clientID `warden-console`, clientSecretEnv `WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`, redirectURL `https://localhost:7070/auth/callback` (matches the Dex client), roles admin [warden-admins], editor [warden-editors], viewer [warden-viewers]. The stack already runs the CP container with TLS on 7070 (lab certs from test/e2e/certs) and `--state-dir /data`.
- Host-side HTTP client in the test: a cookie jar and TLS trusting the lab CA, with no custom dialer and no hosts entry: the browser-style redirect to `http://localhost:5556/dex/...` reaches Dex's published 127.0.0.1:5556 port directly, and `https://localhost:7070` still matches the Dex client's redirect URI. (This replaces the earlier `DialContext` mapping of `dex:5556`, which existed only to reach Dex from the host.)
- Login helper `consoleLogin(t, user)`: GET /auth/login, assert the redirect `Location` starts with `http://localhost:5556/dex/` and never names `dex:5556` (the browser is always sent to the public issuer), follow the redirects to Dex, submit Dex's LDAP login form with the seeded user's password, follow the redirect back through /auth/callback, then read the CSRF token from GET /auth/me. No browser is used. Passwords come from deploy/compose/dex/.env.example and are never printed.
- `TestConsoleSSORoleMatrix`: viewer GET /dashboard/api/traffic 200 and POST /dashboard/api/policy 403; editor PUT policy 2xx and POST settings with an llmProviders change 403 listing the field; only admin POST /dashboard/api/integrations and POST /dashboard/api/secretstore succeed; a POST without X-Warden-CSRF gets 403.
- `TestConsoleSSOSharedTokenRejected`: `Authorization: Bearer <WARDEN_CP_TOKEN>` gets 401 on GET /dashboard/api/settings, POST /dashboard/api/policy and GET/POST /central/secrets, while the same bearer still gets 200 on `/policy` (workers keep pulling).
- `TestConsoleSSORevoke`: an admin DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?sub=<viewer sub> makes the viewer's next request 401 and leaves the admin's session working.
- `TestConsoleSSOSessionFixation`: the cookie set by the callback is `__Host-warden_console`, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure, and its value differs from a cookie value the client presented to /auth/callback beforehand.
- `TestConsoleSSODexDown`: with Dex stopped (`docker compose stop dex`), restart the control-plane container: it still starts and `/policy` still answers 200; `/auth/login` answers 503 `idp_unavailable`; an already-issued session keeps working; after Dex starts again login succeeds (poll up to 60 s for the lazy discovery backoff).
- Test output never prints passwords, cookies, codes or tokens (`make e2e-identity 2>&1 | grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` is 0).

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the console block (with `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556`) to configs/config.e2e-identity-cp.yaml; check the CP container gets WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET (DEX-04 override) and fix the override there if it does not.
2. Add consoleLogin and the cookie-jar client to test/e2e/identity (helpers file), then the five tests.
3. Run `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestConsoleSSO` and iterate; mutate (ignore the CSRF header in a scratch build) to watch the matrix fail.
4. Document the run command next to the role matrix in docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With Docker available, `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestConsoleSSO` passes all subtests; without the stack each test starts with `requireStack(t)` (W-P1-DEX-04), so it fails under `CI=true` and skips loudly otherwise.
- [ ] Given the warden-viewers user, POST /dashboard/api/policy returns 403 and GET /dashboard/api/traffic returns 200; given the shared bearer only, /dashboard/api/settings and /central/secrets return 401 while /policy returns 200 (assertions inside the tests above).
- [ ] Given an admin DELETE of the viewer's sessions, the viewer's next request returns 401 (`TestConsoleSSORevoke`).
- [ ] With Dex stopped and the CP restarted, /policy returns 200 and /auth/login returns 503 `idp_unavailable` (`TestConsoleSSODexDown`).
- [ ] `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity/` is clean, and `scripts/check.sh` (no Docker) passes because the package is behind the e2e tag.
- [ ] `TestConsoleSSORoleMatrix` logging in as alice proves the split-horizon: Dex discovery from the host returns issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex`, the login redirect points at that public issuer, and the CP (which can only reach Dex as `http://dex:5556`) completes the callback and verifies the token. `grep -rnE 'dex[C]lient|Dial[C]ontext|/etc/hosts' test/e2e/identity` prints nothing.
