### 8/11 · W-P1-SSO-08

**Add admin session list and revoke API**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#231](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/231)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). This ticket (#231) lets an admin list live console sessions and revoke one session or every session of a user. The role is computed from the groups stored at login, so a user removed from an IdP group keeps their console role until the session ends (idle 1h, absolute 12h); revocation is the documented manual control, so offboarding does not wait for the 12h expiry. It uses SessionStore.List, Delete and DeleteBySub (W-P1-SSO-04) and the authz table (W-P1-SSO-05); its UI panel uses the api() wrapper (W-P1-SSO-09) and the role-aware hiding (W-P1-SSO-11). W-P2-APIK-03 and W-P3-CSIG-04 extend these routes (API-key revocation by owner, portal sessions). Out of scope: the table and middleware (SSO-05), login, logout of the caller's own session (SSO-09).

What to build: two admin routes mounted by the CP and a panel in the UI. IMPORTANT: the routes are mounted on the CP mux ahead of `dash.Handler()`, so the dashboard's own write guard does NOT run for them; they are wrapped explicitly with withSession and requireRole(admin) (which enforces CSRF on DELETE), and a bearer-only DELETE must get 401.

**Requirements**

- GET /dashboard/api/sessions returns `[{handle, iss, sub, email, authMethod, createdAt, lastSeenAt, expiresAt}]`, where handle is the hex id_hash; the raw id and CSRF token are never returned.
- DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?handle=<hex> revokes one session; DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?sub=<sub> revokes every session for that subject. Unknown handles return 404.
- Both are admin in the authz table and are mounted on the CP mux only in oidc mode (internal/controlplane/routes.go, rule X9), wrapped with withSession + requireRole; because they sit outside `dash.Handler()` the dashboard write guard does not cover them, so the wrapper enforces the session, the admin role and CSRF itself. The authz coverage test includes these CP-added dashboard routes.
- Revocation takes effect on the next request (any in-memory lookup cache is cleared on delete).
- Each revoke logs `msg=console_session_revoked by_sub target_sub count`, never handles in full or cookie values.
- The dashboard gains a Sessions panel for admins listing sessions with a revoke button, using the api() wrapper.
- Mid-session role drift is documented behaviour, not a bug: the role comes from the groups captured at login, so a demoted user keeps their role until idle/absolute expiry or until an admin revokes the session here. The roles docs (W-P1-SSO-11) say the same.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/controlplane/sessions_admin.go (new) with handleSessionsList and handleSessionsRevoke over SessionStore.
2. Mount /dashboard/api/sessions on the CP mux ahead of /dashboard/ in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) in oidc mode, and add it as admin to the table in internal/controlplane/authz.go.
3. Extend the coverage test in internal/controlplane/authz_test.go to include CP-mounted dashboard routes.
4. Add the Sessions panel to internal/dashboard/index.html, shown only when the role is admin.
5. Add internal/controlplane/sessions_admin_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given two sessions for sub A and one for sub B, when an admin sends DELETE ?sub=A, then both A cookies get 401 on the next request and B still works: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionsRevoke`
- [ ] Given an editor, when GET or DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions is sent, then 403
- [ ] The list response contains no raw session id and no csrf field
- [ ] Given none mode, GET /dashboard/api/sessions returns 404
- [ ] Given a bearer-only DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?sub=A (shared or admin token, no session), then 401 and A's sessions are intact: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionsRevokeBearerRefused`
- [ ] Given an admin session without X-Warden-CSRF, DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions gets 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSessionsRevokeNeedsCSRF`
- [ ] The Sessions panel appears in the served index.html only behind `data-min-role="admin"` and calls api(): `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIndexSessionsPanel`
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode; [`W-P1-SSO-09`](console-sso-rbac.md#911--w-p1-sso-09) Add POST /auth/logout, GET /auth/me and the dashboard api() fetch wrapper; [`W-P1-SSO-11`](console-sso-rbac.md#1111--w-p1-sso-11) Make the dashboard UI role-aware and document the role matrix

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#47--w-p3-csig-04) Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation; [`W-P1-SSO-07`](console-sso-rbac.md#711--w-p1-sso-07) Add the L2 Dex-backed console SSO end-to-end test; [`W-P2-APIK-03`](api-keys.md#37--w-p2-apik-03) Add the API key management and self-introspection API

### 9/11 · W-P1-SSO-09

**Add POST /auth/logout, GET /auth/me and the dashboard api() fetch wrapper**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#448](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/448)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). Once sessions exist (W-P1-SSO-04), the browser needs a way to learn who it is, to get its CSRF token and to log out, and the dashboard needs one fetch wrapper that sends that token. This ticket (new, split from the original M ticket #34) adds `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /auth/me` and the UI wrapper. It depends on SSO-04. Siblings: SSO-03 (login), SSO-05 (enforcement), SSO-11 (role-aware UI and docs, which builds on /auth/me), SSO-08 (sessions panel). Other tickets use /auth/me (W-P1-PVER-04 rollback button, W-P1-OPS1-09 break-glass test, W-P2-AREG-03 Agents tab via api()). Out of scope: role enforcement, login.

What to build: two handlers registered in internal/controlplane/routes.go (rule X9) in oidc mode only, and one `api(method, url, body)` wrapper in internal/dashboard/index.html that replaces the direct fetch() calls. In `console.auth: none` the console keeps today's behaviour: dashboard reads are open and every dashboard write is gated by the CP admin bearer through `dashboardWriteGuard` (internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, fail-closed, constant-time, via `dashboard.SetWriteGuard`); that bearer is the separate CP admin token (`--admin-token-env`) delivered by the worker-tokens work, and until it lands the existing shared `--token-env` bearer fills the role. In `console.auth: oidc` sessions and CSRF replace it: the shared tokens never open a human route.

**Requirements**

- `POST /auth/logout` (CSRF checked by withSession) deletes the session row and clears the cookie (same name and flags as set); `GET /auth/me` returns `{sub,email,role,authMethod,csrf,expiresAt}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, or 401. The role is derived with ConsoleConfig.RoleFor from the stored groups and the current config; `csrf` is `CSRFToken(rawID)` from SSO-04. Both routes are mounted only in oidc mode (404 in none mode) from internal/controlplane/routes.go.
- internal/dashboard/index.html: one `api(method, url, body)` wrapper that loads /auth/me once and caches it. If /auth/me returns 200 (oidc mode) it adds `X-Warden-CSRF` on every non-GET call, NEVER prompts for a token, and sends a 401 to `/auth/login?next=<current path>`. If /auth/me returns 404 (none mode) it sends no CSRF header and keeps the existing bearer-prompt behaviour unchanged (the write wrapper near line 1268: token asked once, kept in sessionStorage, retried after 401). Replace the direct fetch() calls with it.
- Logs: `console_logout` carries the first 8 hex characters of the id hash at most, never the cookie or CSRF value.
- No new package or module; the only architecture-visible change is the two routes in routes.go.
- Logout is local: `POST /auth/logout` deletes the Warden session only. It makes no request to the IdP, redirects nowhere and never sends an `id_token_hint`, because no IdP token is stored (W-P1-SSO-03 stores none). The IdP session therefore remains and the next login can be silent. Removing a person's access is the block list's job (W-P1-BLOCK-07 denies console login and sessions for blocked principals; W-P1-BLOCK-05 closes sessions open when a block lands), not logout's. The handler's godoc says this, and docs/identity-dex.md (W-P1-DEX-03) repeats it.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/controlplane/auth_session.go (new): handleLogout and handleMe; register them in internal/controlplane/routes.go in oidc mode.
2. Add the api() wrapper to internal/dashboard/index.html and route every existing fetch() through it, keeping the existing bearer-prompt code reachable only when /auth/me is 404.
3. Add tests in internal/controlplane/auth_session_test.go (new) and internal/dashboard/ui_auth_test.go (extend; served-HTML assertions).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a logged-in user, when POST /auth/logout is sent with CSRF and the old cookie is reused on GET /auth/me, then the response is 401; logout without CSRF gets 403 and keeps the session: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestLogout`
- [ ] GET /auth/me returns sub, email, role, authMethod, csrf and expiresAt with Cache-Control no-store for a viewer, editor and admin session, 401 without a session, and 404 in none mode: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthMe`
- [ ] The served index.html contains the api() wrapper, adds `X-Warden-CSRF` only when /auth/me succeeded, redirects 401 to `/auth/login?next=`, and the bearer-prompt code path is still present and only taken when /auth/me is 404; no `fetch(` call remains outside the wrapper: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIndexAPIWrapper` (fails red-first on the old file).
- [ ] None-mode UI still prompts for the admin token on a 401: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIndexNoneModeBearerPrompt` (static assertion on the served HTML plus the existing ui_auth_test cases).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane` passes and `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] Logout touches only Warden: with a fake IdP counting requests, a logout makes zero requests to it, the response has no `Location` and no `id_token_hint`, and the Dex-side session is untouched (a later /auth/login can complete without a new password prompt in the fake): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestLogoutIsLocal`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#411--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-DEX-03`](dex-oidc.md#36--w-p1-dex-03) Document Dex as Warden's IdP with connector, failure-mode and prod guidance; [`W-P3-CSIG-05`](consent-auth.md#57--w-p3-csig-05) Extract the console OIDC flow and session store into internal/webauth; [`W-P1-SSO-08`](console-sso-rbac.md#811--w-p1-sso-08) Add admin session list and revoke API; [`W-P1-SSO-11`](console-sso-rbac.md#1111--w-p1-sso-11) Make the dashboard UI role-aware and document the role matrix; [`W-P1-PVER-04`](policy-versioning.md#412--w-p1-pver-04) Add history panel with diff view and rollback to dashboard; [`W-P1-OPS1-09`](ops-hardening.md#911--w-p1-ops1-09) Add break-glass startup guards, the session banner and the degraded-mode test; [`W-P2-AREG-03`](agent-registry.md#37--w-p2-areg-03) Add the Agents tab to the CP console

### 10/11 · W-P1-SSO-10

**Authorize settings writes per field and rate-limit query/generate**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#449](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/449)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). SettingsWire carries llmProviders, the secrets selector, identity and other fields that decide where workers send real credentials, so an editor must not be able to change them. W-P1-SSO-05 therefore makes settings writes admin-only (fail-closed); this ticket (new, split from the original M ticket #35) relaxes that to a per-field check so editors can change only the harmless fields, and adds the per-session rate limit on the LLM-spending query/generate route. It depends on SSO-05 (authz table, requireRole, Principal). Siblings: SSO-11 (UI and docs). W-P2-APPR-02, W-P2-WBND-07 and W-P4-HOOK-10 later reuse the editor-field set and add admin-only fields to it. Out of scope: the table itself, UI, docs.

What to build: `settingsFieldsChanged`, the context-aware settings writer, the typed role error, and a token bucket. In none mode nothing changes.

**Requirements**

- Export the editor field set from internal/config (`config.EditorSettingsFields`: advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents, cacheTTLSeconds) so other features share one definition.
- `settingsFieldsChanged(live, in config.SettingsWire) []string` (new, internal/controlplane/authz.go): compares by JSON field. Any difference in a field outside the editor set (llmProviders, secrets, explore, judge, observability, mcp, identity, and any field added later) is reported, and so is any change to an `agents[].identity` value (compare the agents with identity ignored for the editor set, then compare the identity values separately).
- `SetSettingsWriter` in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go changes to `func(context.Context, config.SettingsWire) error`; update the worker call site (it ignores the context), the CP call site and internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go. The CP writer reads the Principal from the context, computes the changed fields against the live SettingsWire and returns a typed `RoleRequiredError{Need config.Role, Fields []string}` when an editor touches an admin field; the settings handler maps it to 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"admin","fields":[...]}`.
- Authz table: POST/PUT settings becomes editor (was admin in SSO-05); the per-field check does the rest. An admin may change any field.
- Rate limit: POST /dashboard/api/query/generate is limited to 10 requests per minute per session (token bucket keyed by the session id hash, injectable clock, bounded memory with idle buckets evicted); the 11th request within a minute gets 429 `{"error":"rate_limited"}` with a Retry-After header. A viewer still gets 403 `role_required` (need editor) before any bucket is touched.
- No new route, package or module.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add config.EditorSettingsFields and its test in internal/config.
2. Add settingsFieldsChanged and RoleRequiredError in internal/controlplane/authz.go; change SetSettingsWriter and its callers; map the error in the dashboard settings handler.
3. Add the token bucket and wire it to the query/generate row.
4. Tests in internal/controlplane/authz_test.go and internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go (update).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Table test of settingsFieldsChanged covers: unchanged, only dlp, llmProviders baseURL, secrets backend, explore, identity block, a new unknown top-level field, and agents[].identity versus agents[].policy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSettingsFieldsChanged`
- [ ] Given an editor, when POST /dashboard/api/settings changes llmProviders[0].baseURL, the secrets backend or agents[0].identity, then 403 lists the field; when it changes only dlp or agents[0].policy, then 2xx; an admin can change all: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzSettingsPerField`
- [ ] Given a viewer, POST /dashboard/api/query/generate gets 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"editor"}`; given an editor, the 11th call within one minute gets 429 and a new minute (fake clock) allows again; two sessions have separate buckets: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzQueryGenerateEditor`
- [ ] Worker dashboard tests pass unchanged with the new writer signature: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/worker`
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-SSO-11`](console-sso-rbac.md#1111--w-p1-sso-11) Make the dashboard UI role-aware and document the role matrix; [`W-P2-APPR-02`](policy-approvals.md#29--w-p2-appr-02) Implement widening-change classification; [`W-P2-WBND-07`](identity-enforcement.md#710--w-p2-wbnd-07) Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability; [`W-P4-HOOK-10`](policy-hooks.md#1011--w-p4-hook-10) Guard hook settings on the CP with validation, roles, audit and capability checks

### 11/11 · W-P1-SSO-11

**Make the dashboard UI role-aware and document the role matrix**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#450](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/450)

Context: feature p1-sso-roles (epic #30). The server is the only enforcement point (SSO-05, SSO-10), but a viewer should not be shown buttons that always fail. This ticket (new, split from the original M ticket #35) hides controls the current role cannot use, shows who is signed in with a logout button, and writes the role matrix and the none-versus-oidc behaviour into docs/control-plane.md. It depends on SSO-05 (table), SSO-09 (/auth/me, logout and the api() wrapper) and SSO-10 (per-field rules to document). Out of scope: server-side enforcement, the sessions admin panel (SSO-08), the none-to-oidc migration guide (SSO-06).

What to build: `data-min-role` handling in internal/dashboard/index.html and a doc section kept in sync with the authz table by a test.

**Requirements**

- internal/dashboard/index.html: controls carry `data-min-role="viewer|editor|admin"`; after /auth/me the UI hides every control whose minimum role is above the user's role; it shows the user's email and role and a logout button (POST /auth/logout through api()). In none mode (/auth/me 404) nothing is hidden and no user chrome is shown. Hiding is cosmetic: the server stays the only enforcement point.
- docs/control-plane.md: a role matrix section (route, method, minimum role, action) between marker comments `<!-- authz-matrix:start -->` and `<!-- authz-matrix:end -->`, generated from the authz table; the editor-versus-admin settings fields; the query/generate rate limit; and the sentence that roles are computed from the groups in the login token and stored with the session, so a user demoted in the IdP keeps their console role until the session's idle (1h) or absolute (12h) expiry unless an admin revokes it with the sessions API (W-P1-SSO-08).
- docs/control-plane.md also states the two modes side by side: none = open reads, writes gated by the CP admin bearer; oidc = sessions and CSRF, the shared tokens never open a human route (no migration steps here; SSO-06 owns them).
- No route, package or module.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add `data-min-role` attributes to the write and admin controls in internal/dashboard/index.html and the show/hide logic driven by /auth/me.
2. Add the matrix generator test helper (`go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzMatrixDoc -update` style, or a plain assertion) and write the docs section.
3. Add tests in internal/dashboard and internal/controlplane.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The served index.html carries `data-min-role` on every write control of the policy, settings, integrations, llmproviders and secretstore tabs, and the hide logic only runs when /auth/me succeeded: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIndexRoleAware`.
- [ ] The matrix in docs/control-plane.md equals the one generated from the authz table, and fails (red first) when a row is added without regenerating: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzMatrixDoc`.
- [ ] `grep -E 'idle|absolute|revoke' docs/control-plane.md` shows the role-drift sentence, and `grep -E 'open reads|CSRF' docs/control-plane.md` shows the two-mode summary.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode; [`W-P1-SSO-09`](console-sso-rbac.md#911--w-p1-sso-09) Add POST /auth/logout, GET /auth/me and the dashboard api() fetch wrapper; [`W-P1-SSO-10`](console-sso-rbac.md#1011--w-p1-sso-10) Authorize settings writes per field and rate-limit query/generate

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-SSO-08`](console-sso-rbac.md#811--w-p1-sso-08) Add admin session list and revoke API
